Bill.BriefDescription: Changing rules for recovery of court costs.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to recovery of court costs; and amending RCW4.84.030.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 4.84.030 and 1987 c 202 s 121 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In any action under Title 26 RCW in the superior court ofWashington the prevailing party shall be entitled to his or her costsand disbursements; but the plaintiff shall in no case be entitled tocosts taxed as attorneys' fees in actions within the jurisdiction ofthe district court when commenced in the superior court. (2) In any action in a court of record in Washington other thanactions under Title 26 RCW, the prevailing or substantially prevailingparty shall be entitled to his or her costs and disbursements,including reasonable attorneys' fees. The court shall determine andaward the amount of reasonable attorneys' fees and costs under thischapter. A party shall be considered to prevail if it obtainssubstantial relief on a material issue or material issues sought.Reasonable attorneys' fees shall be proportionate to the total numberof attorneys' hours necessary to prevail on the material issue or p. 1 SB 5858material issues multiplied by a reasonable hourly rate of compensation.The hourly rate of compensation is presumed reasonable if substantiallysimilar to fees charged by other attorneys in the same area for work ofsimilar substance and complexity.
